image.alt: A person dressed in black writes notes and a schedule on a reMarkable Paper Pro resting on their lap, focusing on one act rather than incoming tablet notifications.

slides.text:
The value of a screen
that cannot do everything

Rather than expanding into a general-purpose tablet, reMarkable Paper Pro narrows its materials, interactions, and connections around reading and writing, creating conditions in which attention can remain with the work.

image.alt: A black Marker tip touches the edge of a gray digital-paper screen with faint handwriting visible, emphasizing the tactile relationship between pen and surface.

slides.text:
Surface friction
becomes part of the interface

Paper Pro's 11.8-inch color digital paper uses a custom-textured surface to create friction closer to pen on paper. The manufacturer says the distance between the pen tip and digital ink is under 1 mm.

The design does more than resemble paper. It aligns the motion of the hand with the response of the screen so attention can __remain with the act of recording__.

image.alt: A hand holds a reMarkable Paper Pro displaying pen types and a color palette over a document, showing how Canvas Color organizes notes and annotations.

slides.text:
Color is used to create structure,
not stimulation

The Canvas Color display uses millions of colored ink particles. Color can separate notes and plans, mark directly on documents, and reveal the hierarchy of important information.

Here, color is not decoration designed to prolong engagement. It functions more like an information structure that helps people organize and retrieve thought.

image.alt:
The screen's light should
adapt to its environment

slides.text:
The screen's light should
adapt to its environment

Unlike the emissive display of a phone or laptop, Paper Pro uses digital paper that reflects ambient light. In darker spaces, a reading light with adjustable brightness can be switched on as support.

Instead of always offering the brightest screen, it creates __conditions for reading with the light already around us__. That connects directly to Calm Technology's treatment of light.

image.alt: A person sits in a sunlit room looking at a reMarkable Paper Pro, remaining with the current task in a quiet environment.

slides.text:
Focus begins with boundaries,
not features

Paper Pro centers its functions on notebooks, documents, and handwriting. It does less than a general-purpose tablet, but it also creates fewer paths from the current task to messages, video, and feeds.

No device can focus on our behalf. What matters is __not only what the product includes, but which transitions it refuses to make easy__.

image.alt: Amber Case holds a reMarkable Paper Pro displaying a Calm Tech Certified document while another representative stands beside her.

slides.text:
Evaluation covered
the entire experience

Paper Pro received Calm Tech Certified™ in 2024. The Institute says it followed the experience from purchase and unboxing through setup and everyday use, examining attention, periphery, durability, light, sound, and materials.

Certification is not a guarantee of focus. It is __a signal that the product was systematically reviewed for how its design treats human attention__.

image.alt:
Instead of more features,
what tool would protect
__one action you value?__

slides.text:
Instead of more features,
what tool would protect
__one action you value?__

caption.body: reMarkable Paper Pro does not reject digital technology. It brings forward only the capabilities needed for reading and writing. Paper-like friction, a reflective color display, and a limited functional scope cannot create focus for us, but they can create the conditions for it. Calm Technology asks not how many features a device contains, but what boundaries it designs to protect a particular action.
caption.cta: Instead of more features, what tool would protect one action you value?
